## Step 1: Apply the Euclidean Algorithm

Find gcd(1001, 10):

| Step | Dividend | Divisor | Quotient | Remainder |
|------|----------|---------|----------|-----------|
| 1 | 1001 | 10 | 100 | 1 |
| 2 | 10 | 1 | 10 | 0 |

Since gcd(1001, 10) = 1, the inverse exists.

## Step 2: Back-Substitute (Extended Euclidean)

From Step 1:
$$1 = 1001 - 100 \times 10$$

This gives us directly:
$$1 \equiv -100 \times 10 \pmod{1001}$$

## Step 3: Solve for the Inverse

$$10^{-1} \equiv -100 \pmod{1001}$$

Converting to a positive integer in [0, 1000]:
$$-100 + 1001 = \boxed{901}$$

## Verification

$$10 \times 901 = 9010 = 9 \times 1001 + 1 \equiv 1 \pmod{1001} \checkmark$$

The modular inverse of 10 modulo 1001 is **901**.
